name: @kitora/charts
description: Kitora's charts on plain SVG: line, area, bar (grouped, stacked, horizontal), combined, pie and donut, radar, radial bar, gauge, funnel, scatter, sparkline and heatmap, plus a ranked bars list in HTML, with axes, legends, crosshair tooltips, a table fallback, keyboard reading, SVG and PNG export and light and dark palettes. Scale and shape maths live in the kit; no chart library.

exports.name: bandScale
exports.description:
A band scale over `domain` keys. `paddingInner` is the gap between bands as a fraction of the step;
`paddingOuter` the space before the first and after the last band, in steps.
exports.signature: (domain: readonly string[], range: readonly [number, number], paddingInner?: number, paddingOuter?: number) => BandScale

exports.name: clamp
exports.description: Limits `value` to the range `[lo, hi]`.
exports.signature: (value: number, lo: number, hi: number) => number

exports.name: DEFAULT_TICK_COUNT
exports.description: The default tick count an axis asks for when it is not told; about one tick per 60–80px at chart sizes.

exports.name: linearScale
exports.description: A linear scale from `domain` to `range`; a zero-width domain maps everything to the range midpoint.
exports.signature: (domain: readonly [number, number], range: readonly [number, number]) => LinearScale

exports.name: niceDomain
exports.description: Widens a domain outward to whole tick steps, so the axis starts and ends on a labelled tick.
exports.signature: (start: number, stop: number, count?: number) => [number, number]

exports.name: niceTicks
exports.description: Evenly spaced nice ticks inside `[start, stop]` (inclusive), ascending.
exports.signature: (start: number, stop: number, count?: number) => number[]

exports.name: tickStep
exports.description:
The tick step for `count` ticks across `[start, stop]`: 1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten, the same
"nice" steps d3 uses, so axis labels read 0, 20, 40 rather than 0, 17.3, 34.6.
exports.signature: (start: number, stop: number, count: number) => number

exports.name: timeTicks
exports.description: Time ticks: calendar-aligned instants (midnight, the 1st of a month, Jan 1) inside `[start, stop]`, local time (UTC with `utc`).
exports.signature: (start: number, stop: number, count?: number, options?: TimeTicksOptions) => { ticks: number[]; unit: TimeUnit; }

exports.name: BandScale
exports.description: A categorical scale: each key owns one band of equal width, separated by padding.

exports.name: LinearScale
exports.description: A continuous scale: number → pixel, with the ticks an axis should draw.

exports.name: TimeTicksOptions
exports.description: Options for `timeTicks`.

exports.name: TimeUnit
exports.description: The calendar unit a time axis ticks on: minute, hour, day, month or year.

exports.name: arcGeometry
exports.description:
The one arc drawing behind feedback's `CircularProgress` and `Meter.Ring` and the charts kit's `GaugeChart`: a circle of
radius `(size - thickness) / 2` centred in a `size` box, painted from `startAngle` by a dash of the arc's length offset by
the unpainted share. A full sweep gives exactly the circle and dash those rings have always drawn (`strokeDasharray` = 2πr,
`strokeDashoffset` = 2πr × (1 − fraction)); a partial sweep (a 240° dial) uses the same radius rule, caps and dash.
A reversed sweep (end before start) is treated as empty.
exports.signature: ({ size, thickness, startAngle, endAngle, fraction }: ArcGeometryOptions) => ArcGeometry

exports.name: arcPath
exports.description:
An annular sector path centred on the origin. `inner` 0 draws a pie wedge; angles are radians clockwise
from 12 o'clock. A full circle is drawn as two half arcs, since one SVG arc cannot close on itself.
exports.signature: (inner: number, outer: number, startAngle: number, endAngle: number) => string

exports.name: areaPath
exports.description:
A closed area between a top line and a baseline; `bottom` is per point (a stacked area's lower edge)
and must have the same length as `top`. A null in either breaks the area.
exports.signature: (top: readonly (Point | null)[], bottom: readonly (Point | null)[], curve?: Curve) => string

exports.name: barPath
exports.description:
A bar rectangle with its two corners at `end` rounded by `radius` (clamped to fit), so bars read as
anchored to the baseline and rounded only where the value ends.
exports.signature: (x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, radius: number, end: BarEnd) => string

exports.name: CURVES
exports.description: Every curve, for pickers and validation.

exports.name: linePath
exports.description: One SVG path for a polyline; each run of non-null points becomes its own subpath, so gaps stay gaps.
exports.signature: (points: readonly (Point | null)[], curve?: Curve) => string

exports.name: pieLayout
exports.description:
Lays values around a circle in input order (callers sort when they want largest first). Negative and
non-finite values count as zero: a pie cannot show them, and silently flipping them would lie.
exports.signature: (values: readonly number[], padAngle?: number) => PieSlice[]

exports.name: polar
exports.description: A point at `radius` and `angle` (radians clockwise from 12 o'clock), in SVG coordinates (y down).
exports.signature: (radius: number, angle: number) => [number, number]

exports.name: ArcGeometry
exports.description: A stroked arc: its circle, its length, the track path and the dash that paints a share of it.

exports.name: ArcGeometryOptions
exports.description: Options of `arcGeometry`: a stroked arc in a `size` × `size` box.

exports.name: BarEnd
exports.description: Which end of a bar carries the rounded corners: the data end, away from the baseline.

exports.name: Curve
exports.description:
How a line passes through its points. `monotone` is a smooth curve that never overshoots a data
point (no fake peaks between samples, unlike a plain cubic); `step` holds each value until the next.

exports.name: PieSlice
exports.description: One slice of a pie layout: its angles in radians, clockwise from 12 o'clock.

exports.name: Point
exports.description: A point in pixels; `null` coordinates break a line (a gap for a missing value).

exports.name: angleDistance
exports.description: The smallest angular distance between two angles, 0..π.
exports.signature: (a: number, b: number) => number

exports.name: angleLabelAnchor
exports.description: The anchor of a label for `angle` at `radius` from the centre, for text `fontSize` px tall.
exports.signature: (angle: number, radius: number, fontSize?: number) => AngleLabelAnchor

exports.name: buildPolarModel
exports.description: Categories, series values, the table (categories as rows, series as columns), the summary and the legend.
exports.signature: <T>(options: PolarOptions<T>, hidden: ReadonlySet<string>, adapters: ChartAdapters) => PolarModel<T>

exports.name: buildRadialBarModel
exports.description: Bars in drawing order (input order, or largest first), the table (label, value, share of max), the summary and the legend.
exports.signature: <T>(options: RadialBarOptions<T>, adapters: ChartAdapters) => RadialBarModel<T>

exports.name: gridRingPath
exports.description: A grid ring (centred on the origin) as a closed path. A polygon needs at least three angles; fewer falls back to a circle.
exports.signature: (r: number, angles: readonly number[], shape: PolarGridShape) => string

exports.name: layoutPolar
exports.description:
The radar layout at a size: the circle fits `min(width, height)`, shrunk so the measured category labels fit beside it
(down to half the half-size, after which labels truncate with an ellipsis), then rings, spokes, labels, radius ticks
and one closed shape per visible series. Empty data gives an empty layout with no NaN anywhere.
exports.signature: <T>(model: PolarModel<T>, options: PolarLayoutOptions, adapters: ChartAdapters) => PolarLayout

exports.name: layoutRadialBars
exports.description:
The radial bar layout: the circle fits `min(width, height)`, one ring per bar from the outside in (the first row
outermost), each bar's track the full sweep and its value arc from the start to the value's angle, and each name at
the bar's start on the side the sweep leaves open. Empty data gives an empty layout with no NaN anywhere.
exports.signature: <T>(model: RadialBarModel<T>, options: RadialBarLayoutOptions, adapters: ChartAdapters) => PolarLayout

exports.name: MISSING_TEXT
exports.description: The word a missing value reads as in the readout and the table.

exports.name: nearestSpoke
exports.description: The index of the category whose spoke is nearest a point (relative to the centre), or null beyond `maxRadius` or with no categories.
exports.signature: (x: number, y: number, angles: readonly number[], maxRadius: number) => number | null

exports.name: pointAngle
exports.description: The angle of a point relative to the centre, clockwise from 12 o'clock, 0..2π.
exports.signature: (x: number, y: number) => number

exports.name: POLAR_GRID_SHAPES
exports.description: Every grid shape, for pickers and validation.

exports.name: polarAnchor
exports.description: Where the tooltip anchors for the category at `index`, in plot pixels: the outermost visible point on its spoke (a radar), the end of its bar (a radial bar).
exports.signature: (layout: PolarLayout, index: number) => { x: number; y: number; } | null

exports.name: polarAngles
exports.description:
The angle of each of `count` categories, evenly around `startAngle`..`endAngle`. A full turn (the default, from 12
o'clock) puts them `turn / count` apart, so the last does not land on the first; a partial sweep puts the first at the
start and the last at the end.
exports.signature: (count: number, startAngle?: number, endAngle?: number) => number[]

exports.name: polarHitIndex
exports.description: The category under a point given in plot pixels (from the plot's top-left), or null: the nearest spoke on a radar, the ring under the point on a radial bar.
exports.signature: (layout: PolarLayout, x: number, y: number) => number | null

exports.name: polarReadout
exports.description: What a reader hears and sees for the category at `index`: "Speed: Model A 7, Model B 5" over the visible series.
exports.signature: <T>(model: PolarModel<T>, index: number) => Readout | null

exports.name: radarPath
exports.description: A closed path through a series' points (the radar shape); empty with no points.
exports.signature: (points: readonly Point[]) => string

exports.name: radarPoints
exports.description: The points of one series: each value at its category's angle, a missing value (null, NaN) at the centre.
exports.signature: (values: readonly (number | null | undefined)[], angles: readonly number[], scale: LinearScale) => RadarPoint[]

exports.name: radialBarHitIndex
exports.description: The bar whose ring is under a point in plot pixels (anywhere along its track), or null.
exports.signature: (layout: PolarLayout, x: number, y: number) => number | null

exports.name: radialBarReadout
exports.description: What a reader hears and sees for the bar at `index`: "Storage: 72 of 100, 72%".
exports.signature: <T>(model: RadialBarModel<T>, index: number) => Readout | null

exports.name: radialScale
exports.description:
The radial value scale: `domain` when given, otherwise a nice `0..max` (or `min..max` when values go below zero), with
`rings` evenly spaced grid values when given and nice ticks otherwise. The centre is the domain's start.
exports.signature: (values: readonly number[], radius: number, options?: { readonly domain?: readonly [number, number]; readonly rings?: number; }) => RadialScale

exports.name: roundedArcPath
exports.description:
An annular sector with semicircular ends (a bar along a ring with round caps), centred on the origin. The caps stay
inside `startAngle`..`endAngle`: the straight part is shortened by each cap, and a sweep too short for two caps draws
one round dot at the start. Empty for a zero sweep or no thickness.
exports.signature: (inner: number, outer: number, startAngle: number, endAngle: number) => string

exports.name: truncateLabel
exports.description: Shortens `label` with an ellipsis until `measure` says it fits `maxWidth`; returns it whole when it fits, "…" at worst.
exports.signature: (label: string, maxWidth: number, measure: TextMeasure) => string

exports.name: AngleLabelAnchor
exports.description: Where an angle label sits and how it is anchored: left of centre it ends at the spoke, right of it it starts there.

exports.name: PolarAngleLabel
exports.description: A category label outside the outer ring; `text` is truncated to fit, `full` is the whole name (shown as a `<title>`).

exports.name: PolarGridShape
exports.description: How grid rings are drawn: true circles, or polygons through the spokes (the classic radar web).

exports.name: PolarLayout
exports.description: The size-dependent geometry every polar part draws from; coordinates of marks are relative to the centre (`cx`, `cy`).

exports.name: PolarLayoutOptions
exports.description: Options of `layoutPolar`.

exports.description: Everything about a polar chart that does not depend on its size.

exports.name: PolarOptions
exports.description: What the polar model needs: one row per category, the series read from each row. The React props extend this.

exports.name: PolarRadiusTick
exports.description: A radius-axis label, placed along the first spoke.

exports.name: PolarRing
exports.description: A grid ring with its value (the radius axis labels one per ring).

exports.name: PolarSeries
exports.description: One series of the model with its values per category.

exports.name: PolarSpoke
exports.description: A spoke from the centre to the outer ring at a category's angle.

exports.name: RadarMark
exports.description: One visible series drawn as a radar shape.

exports.name: RadarPoint
exports.description: One series' points around the categories; a missing value is drawn at the centre and flagged.

exports.name: RadialBarLayoutOptions
exports.description: Options of `layoutRadialBars`.

exports.name: RadialBarMark
exports.description: One bar of a radial bar chart: its ring, its track (the full sweep) and its value arc, with the label at its start.

exports.name: RadialBarModel
exports.description: The radial bar model: a polar model with one series (the value) plus the full-sweep value and each bar's colour and share.

exports.name: RadialBarOptions
exports.description: What the radial bar model needs: one row per bar.

exports.name: RadialScale
exports.description: The value ticks and the radial scale of a polar plot.

exports.name: buildBarsListModel
exports.description: Sorts (unless `sort` is false), cuts to `limit`, and sizes each bar against `max` or the largest value.
exports.signature: <T>(options: BarsListOptions<T>, adapters: ChartAdapters) => BarsListModel<T>

exports.name: BarsListModel
exports.description: The rows shown, how many were left out, the full-bar value, the table and the summary.

exports.name: BarsListOptions
exports.description: What the bars list model needs.

exports.name: BarsListRow
exports.description: One row as drawn.

exports.name: buildFunnelModel
exports.description: Stages in order with their shares of the first and the previous stage, the table, the summary.
exports.signature: <T>(options: FunnelOptions<T>, adapters: ChartAdapters) => FunnelModel<T>

exports.name: funnelHitIndex
exports.description: The stage under a point in plot pixels: the band along the funnel's axis, across the whole plot.
exports.signature: (layout: FunnelLayout, x: number, y: number) => number | null

exports.name: funnelLabelText
exports.description: The text of a stage's value label.
exports.signature: <T>(model: FunnelModel<T>, index: number, labels: FunnelLabels, percentOf: "first" | "previous") => string

exports.name: funnelReadout
exports.description: "Signed up 1,240 · 31% of Visitors · 62% of the previous step", with tooltip rows for the same three facts.
exports.signature: <T>(model: FunnelModel<T>, index: number) => Readout | null

exports.name: layoutFunnel
exports.description:
The funnel at a size. Stage widths (heights when horizontal) are shares of the largest stage, never reordered. A value
label sits inside its stage when it fits, else beside it on the inline-end side when there is room, else centred on the
stage over a pill, clamped to the plot, so no label ever leaves the plot.
exports.signature: <T>(model: FunnelModel<T>, options: FunnelLayoutOptions, adapters: ChartAdapters) => FunnelLayout

exports.name: FunnelLabels
exports.description: What the label on each stage shows.

exports.name: FunnelLayout
exports.description: The funnel layout.

exports.name: FunnelLayoutOptions
exports.description: Options of `layoutFunnel`.

exports.name: FunnelMark
exports.description: One stage at a size: its shape, its band (for hit testing and the active highlight) and its value label.

exports.name: FunnelModel
exports.description: The funnel's size-free model.

exports.name: FunnelOptions
exports.description: What the funnel model needs: one row per stage, in order.

exports.name: FunnelShape
exports.description: How a funnel is drawn.

exports.name: FunnelStage
exports.description: One stage with its shares.

exports.name: layoutGauge
exports.description: The gauge's geometry: the value clamped into min..max, the shared arc with that share painted, the bands and the trimmed box.
exports.signature: (options: GaugeOptions) => GaugeLayout

exports.name: sweepExtent
exports.description: The y extent (top, bottom) of a sweep on the unit circle, y down: the end points and any of 12 / 6 o'clock inside it.
exports.signature: (startAngle: number, endAngle: number) => { top: number; bottom: number; }

exports.name: GaugeBand
exports.description: One band drawn on the track.

exports.name: GaugeLayout
exports.description: The gauge at a size: the track and value geometry, the bands, the clamped value and the box it needs.

exports.name: GaugeOptions
exports.description: What `layoutGauge` needs. Angles are radians clockwise from 12 o'clock.

exports.name: GaugeSegment
exports.description: A coloured band on the gauge's track, from the previous band's end (or the minimum) up to `to`.

exports.name: normaliseColumns
exports.description: Rescales each row of `columns` to shares of its row total (0–1), for 100% stacks; an all-zero row stays zero.
exports.signature: (columns: readonly (readonly (number | null)[])[]) => (number | null)[][]

exports.name: stackColumns
exports.description:
Stacks `columns` (one array of values per series, all the same length as the data) in order.
Positive values grow up from zero and negative values grow down from zero on their own baselines,
so a mixed stack (profit and loss) diverges from the axis instead of overlapping (d3's stackOffsetDiverging).
A missing value takes no space and yields `null`, so the series above it stays put.
exports.signature: (columns: readonly (readonly (number | null)[])[]) => StackedSpans[]

exports.name: StackedSpans
exports.description: One series' spans after stacking, aligned with the data rows; `null` where the value is missing.

exports.name: axisFormatter
exports.description: One axis' tick formatter (the default formats' `axis`).
exports.signature: (ticks: readonly number[]) => (value: number) => string

exports.name: createIntlFormats
exports.description: The default `ChartFormats` on Intl, for one locale (the reader's when omitted) and one time zone (the system's when omitted).
exports.signature: (options?: IntlFormatsOptions) => ChartFormats

exports.name: DEFAULT_FORMATS
exports.description: The formats charts use when no `ChartConfigProvider` supplies others: Intl in the reader's locale.

exports.name: formatCompact
exports.description: Short numbers for ticks (the default formats' `compact`).
exports.signature: (value: number) => string

exports.name: formatDate
exports.description: A date at an axis granularity (the default formats' `date`).
exports.signature: (value: Date | number, unit?: DateUnit) => string

exports.name: formatDateLong
exports.description: A full date (the default formats' `dateLong`).
exports.signature: (value: Date | number) => string

exports.name: formatNumber
exports.description: Full numbers (the default formats' `number`).
exports.signature: (value: number) => string

exports.name: formatPercent
exports.description: A share as a percentage (the default formats' `percent`).
exports.signature: (value: number) => string

exports.name: ChartFormats
exports.description:
The formatting seam every chart reads through. `createIntlFormats` builds one for any locale; pass your
own object (via `ChartConfigProvider` or a chart's `formatValue` / `formatX` props) for anything else.

exports.name: DateUnit
exports.description: The granularities a date axis labels at (see `timeTicks`).

exports.name: IntlFormatsOptions
exports.description: Options for `createIntlFormats`: the locale, the time zone, and extra Intl options for plain numbers (a currency, a unit).

exports.name: nearestIndex
exports.description: The index in ascending `positions` closest to `target` (binary search); -1 for an empty list.
exports.signature: (positions: readonly number[], target: number) => number

exports.name: nearestPoint
exports.description: The index of the point nearest `(x, y)` within `radius` pixels, or -1; for scatter plots.
exports.signature: (points: readonly { x: number; y: number; }[], x: number, y: number, radius: number) => number

exports.name: linearRegression
exports.description: The best-fit line `y = slope·x + intercept` through the points, or null when it is undefined (fewer than two distinct x).
exports.signature: (points: readonly { x: number; y: number; }[]) => { slope: number; intercept: number; } | null

exports.name: createPalette
exports.description: A palette from your own colours (any CSS colour); `sequential` defaults to mixing the first colour into the surface.
exports.signature: (colors: readonly string[], options?: { sequential?: (t: number) => string; other?: string; }) => ChartPalette

exports.name: DEFAULT_PALETTE
exports.description: The kit's palette on the `--dkc-*` tokens.

exports.name: SERIES_COLORS
exports.description:
The categorical slots in their fixed order: blue, orange, aqua, yellow, magenta, green, violet, red.
The order is the colour-blind safety mechanism (adjacent slots stay distinguishable under the common
colour-vision deficiencies), so series take slots in order and are never cycled past eight.

exports.name: SERIES_SLOTS
exports.description: The number of categorical slots; a ninth series should fold into "Other" rather than reuse a colour.

exports.name: seriesColor
exports.description: The colour for the series at `index`; past the last slot it falls back to the muted ink, never a repeat.
exports.signature: (index: number) => string

exports.name: sequentialColor
exports.description:
A sequential (one hue, light → dark) colour for a 0–1 magnitude, mixed in OKLCH between the surface-side
and the deep end of the ramp, so a heatmap reads lighter = less in both themes.
exports.signature: (t: number) => string

exports.name: ChartPalette
exports.description:
The colour seam: how a chart turns a series position or a 0–1 magnitude into a CSS colour. The default
reads the `--dkc-*` tokens; `createPalette` builds one from any list (a brand palette, a monochrome ramp).

exports.name: CHAR_WIDTH
exports.description: Average advance of a tabular digit at TICK_FONT in the Geist / system sans.

exports.name: ESTIMATE_MEASURE
exports.description: The default `TextMeasure`: the character-count estimate.

exports.name: labelWidth
exports.description: The width a list of labels needs, estimated from their length (no DOM, so SSR lays out the same).
exports.signature: (labels: readonly string[]) => number

exports.name: thinTicks
exports.description:
Thins labels so they do not collide: keeps every k-th tick where k is the smallest step that leaves
`minGap` pixels between neighbours. The first tick always stays.
exports.signature: (ticks: readonly Tick[], minGap: number, axis?: "x" | "y", measure?: TextMeasure) => Tick[]

exports.name: TICK_FONT
exports.description: Font size of tick labels in pixels; the default estimate assumes it.

exports.name: TextMeasure
exports.description: The measuring seam: the pixel width the widest of `labels` needs at the tick font.

exports.name: Tick
exports.description: One labelled tick: its pixel position along the axis and its text.

exports.name: DEFAULT_ADAPTERS
exports.description: The kit's defaults: Intl in the reader's locale, the `--dkc-*` palette, the character-count estimate.

exports.name: resolveAdapters
exports.description: The defaults with `overrides` on top; `formats` merges per function, so one can swap only `number`.
exports.signature: (overrides?: { formats?: Partial<ChartFormats>; palette?: ChartPalette; measure?: TextMeasure; }, base?: ChartAdapters) => ChartAdapters

exports.name: ChartAdapters
exports.description: The adapters a chart reads through: formatting, colour and text measurement.

exports.name: toggleHidden
exports.description: The next hidden-set after toggling `key`; the last visible key cannot be hidden (an empty plot reads as "no data").
exports.signature: (hidden: ReadonlySet<string>, key: string, keys: readonly string[]) => ReadonlySet<string>

exports.name: ChartTable
exports.description: A data table: the chart's numbers for screen readers, and for anyone who toggles to the table view.

exports.name: LegendItem
exports.description: One legend entry. `hidden` greys it out; clicking toggles it when the chart allows hiding series.

exports.name: LegendMark
exports.description: The swatch shape of a series: a filled square for areas and bars, a short line for lines.

exports.name: LegendPosition
exports.description: Where a chart's legend sits; `none` hides it (a single series never needs one: the title names it).

exports.name: Readout
exports.description: What a reader hears and sees for the active item: the tooltip title, its rows and the announced sentence.

exports.name: TooltipRow
exports.description: One row of a tooltip.

exports.name: activePoints
exports.description: The active point of each line or area at row `index`.
exports.signature: <T>(model: CartesianModel<T>, layout: CartesianLayout, index: number) => DotMark[]

exports.name: BAR_LAYOUTS
